title: Electric Cells, Resistance and Circuits
summary: Electric cells as energy systems, current, potential difference and resistance, factors affecting resistance, and current and voltage in series and parallel circuits.

notes.text: An **electric cell** converts stored **chemical potential energy** into **electrical energy**. It has a positive terminal and a negative terminal; when connected in a closed circuit, chemical reactions inside the cell push charges around the circuit. A **battery** is two or more cells connected together.

rows: The rate of flow of charge
The energy given to or used by each unit of charge; also called voltage
Voltmeter, connected in **parallel** across a component
How much a component opposes the current

notes.title: Calculating resistance
notes.problem: A potential difference of 6 V across a resistor causes a current of 0,5 A. Calculate the resistance.

notes.text: When charges move through a conductor, they collide with the atoms of the material. This opposition is **resistance**, and it converts electrical energy into **heat** (and sometimes light). A high resistance lets less current flow.

notes.caption: Factors that affect the resistance of a wire
rows: A longer wire has more resistance
A thinner wire has more resistance
Nichrome has high resistance; copper has very low resistance
For most metals, resistance increases as temperature rises

notes.text: High resistance is useful in **heating elements** (kettles, toasters, stoves) and **light bulb filaments**. Copper is used for connecting wires because its low resistance wastes little energy. A **rheostat** (variable resistor) changes resistance by changing the length of wire in the circuit, for example in a dimmer switch.

items: The **current is the same** at every point: $I_{\text{total}} = I_1 = I_2$.
The **potential difference is shared**: $V_{\text{total}} = V_1 + V_2$.
Adding more resistors **increases** the total resistance, so the current **decreases**.
The **current splits** between the branches: $I_{\text{total}} = I_1 + I_2$.
The **potential difference is the same** across each branch: $V_{\text{total}} = V_1 = V_2$.
Adding more resistors in parallel **decreases** the total resistance, so the total current from the battery **increases**.

notes.title: Reading meters in a parallel circuit
notes.problem: Two bulbs are in parallel with a 9 V battery. The current through bulb 1 is 0,3 A and through bulb 2 is 0,6 A. Find the total current and the voltage across bulb 2.
steps: Voltage is the same across each parallel branch: 9 V

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: Remember: **series shares voltage; parallel shares current**.

questions.prompt: Why is nichrome used for the heating element in a kettle while copper is used for the cable?
questions.memo:
✓ Nichrome has high resistance, so it converts electrical energy into heat (1)
✓ Copper has low resistance, so very little energy is wasted in the cable (1)

questions.prompt: What happens to the total current from the battery when another bulb is added in parallel? Explain.
questions.memo:
✓ The total current increases (1)
✓ because the total resistance of the circuit decreases (there is another path for the current) (1)
